commit_message: GATE-10: Android north-star — VPNService adapter, permission, reconnect, battery, reproducible test script
scope_completed: VpnPermissionManager: Android VPN permission state machine (NOT_REQUESTED→REQUESTING→GRANTED/DENIED/REVOKED)
NetworkTracker: Android network connectivity (WIFI/MOBILE_DATA/NONE/SHARENET_ONLY, north-star = NONE)
BatteryManager: battery state (CHARGING/NORMAL/LOW/CRITICAL/DOZE) with adaptive keepalive (30s/60s/120s)
AndroidVpnLifecycle: extends ProcessLifecycle with permission, network, battery integration
Permission revocation → CRASHED + kill-switch blocks (safety property)
Network lost → DEGRADED (reconnect) or STOPPED (critical battery preservation)
NORTH_STAR_TEST_SCRIPT: 10 reproducible ADB steps (mobile data OFF, Wi-Fi OFF, Chrome HTTPS, repeat 3x)
NorthStarTestResult type for documenting device test outcomes
protocol_adr_references: spec/16-platforms.md §1 (platform adapters must NOT create protocol semantics)
spec/00 §39 (North-star: Android mobile data OFF + Wi-Fi OFF + Chrome → ShareNet → real HTTPS)
known_limitations: Actual device test (mobile data OFF + Wi-Fi OFF + Chrome reaches real HTTPS through ShareNet) is DEFERRED — it requires a physical Android device with the ShareNet app installed, ADB access, and the full real-process stack (3-message handshake → circuit → gateway forwarding → VPNService → Chrome). The unit tests prove the adapter abstraction and lifecycle correctness. The NORTH_STAR_TEST_SCRIPT is a reproducible 10-step procedure ready for execution on a real device.

The AndroidVpnLifecycle is an abstraction in reference/platform/ — it does not call real Android APIs (VpnService, ConnectivityManager, BatteryManager). A platform/android/ implementation would bridge these to the real Android SDK.
The NORTH_STAR_TEST_SCRIPT uses ADB commands that require root or developer-mode access on the device. On non-rooted devices, some steps (svc data disable) may require manual toggling via Settings.
